chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Walid (may God be pleased with them) and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris, both, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bizanti, who said: I asked Abul Hasan (peace be upon him)
about the grave of Fatimah (peace be upon her), so he said: She was buried in her house. When the Banu Umayya added to the mosque, her grave became part of the mosque.
ai.seo_question: Where is the grave of Fatimah (peace be upon her) located according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her) was originally buried in her private residence, a location that was later incorporated into the mosque structure during the Umayyad expansion. This narration provides crucial historical context for the scholarly debate regarding whether her grave is within the mosque itself or adjacent to it, affirming the sanctity of her dwelling as a place of worship.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-71 My father, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bezanti that he asked Abul Hassan Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s)
about the location of the tomb of Fatima (s). The Imam (s) said, “She (s) was buried in her own house. When the Umayyads added onto the mosque, her grave became a part of the mosque.”
